title: Closed‑Loop Vagus Nerve Stimulation: Modal Stratification, Multimodal Triggering, and Clinical Translational Evidence
content: Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is an established bioelectronic therapy for neurological, inflammatory, and autonomic disorders. Conventional open‑loop systems, however, lack a unifying mechanistic framework, with limited regulatory precision and heterogeneous therapeutic efficacy. This review formalizes a dual‑axis regulatory framework with the nucleus tractus solitarii (NTS) as its principal hub, constituting the pathophysiological foundation for next‑generation closed‑loop VNS. It delineates two functionally distinct axes: an afferent‑dominant ascending brain axis mediating central neuromodulation and neuroplastic remodeling, and an efferent‑dominant descending somatic axis driving peripheral anti‑inflammation and autonomic homeostasis. Evidence‑based criteria for defining functional axis dominance across disease types and stages are established. Grounded in this framework, we outline a stratified closed‑loop VNS architecture encompassing pathology‑matched trigger strategies, pathway‑aligned stimulation paradigms, and a full‑course invasive–non‑invasive synergistic treatment paradigm. Clinical evidence from drug‑resistant epilepsy and spinal cord injury cohorts confirms that mechanism‑aligned closed‑loop VNS yields superior therapeutic outcomes over open‑loop stimulation. This work bridges the longstanding gap between mechanistic research and engineering development in VNS, providing a systematic roadmap for precision bioelectronic therapy advancement and clinical translation.
